objective: Help readers retain their place while long-form audit sections enter the viewport during a normal document scroll.

elements.target: Reveal component wrappers below the hero

spatial_relationship: Content begins twelve pixels below its reserved final position and settles in the document flow.

selection_rationale.escalation_reason: The product owner explicitly requires Framer scroll animation for this deliverable; the effect stays inside the already selected React motion layer and does not introduce a second engine.

rejected_alternatives.why_not: It would not meet the explicit request for a Framer-animated scroll experience.
It still needs visibility lifecycle state and would duplicate the motion layer already required by the deliverable.
It would create a second imperative lifecycle path for an effect already owned by the React component tree.

sequence.target: Reveal component wrappers below the hero

timing.derivation: The travel distance is only twelve pixels and the content is read once, so 360ms provides orientation without delaying comprehension or making every block feel staged.

easing.character: Quiet deceleration that feels editorial and controlled rather than springy or decorative.

interruption.notes: Viewport animations run once; rapid scrolling may cancel an unseen entrance while the readable final state is retained.

responsive.mobile: Use the same twelve-pixel maximum travel with no viewport-relative distance.
responsive.tablet: Use the same reserved-space opacity and transform effect.
responsive.desktop: Use the same reserved-space opacity and transform effect.
responsive.orientation_or_input_notes: No hover behavior or scroll interception is used; native touch and keyboard scrolling remain intact.

reduced_motion.implementation: MotionConfig reducedMotion user removes transforms, while useReducedMotion selects a 120ms opacity-only state.
reduced_motion.vestibular_review: No parallax, zoom, spin, scroll hijacking or large-area travel is present; the reduced branch removes all translation.

keyboard_and_focus.focus_behavior: The wrappers never take or move focus, and focus indicators remain visible and outside the animated properties.

ssr.hydration_notes: The standalone Vite build is client-rendered; the hero is not wrapped in Reveal and remains visible before any below-fold effect begins.

cleanup.on_unmount: Motion owns and cancels its viewport animations when React unmounts each component.
cleanup.listeners_and_observers: Motion owns the viewport observer and scroll subscription; no manual listener or observer is created by Reveal.
cleanup.route_change_notes: The standalone site has no client-side routes; the main app route unmounts the page normally.

performance_budget.cls_contribution: None expected because every wrapper reserves its final document space and only opacity and transform animate.
performance_budget.notes: Framer Motion was already added for the original deliverable; the standalone bundle delta is measured in the verification report.

acceptance_criteria: Above-the-fold hero text is visible immediately on every cold load.
Every below-fold Reveal reaches opacity one after entering the viewport.
Reduced motion removes translateY while preserving every content end state.
No viewport from 320 to 1440 pixels shows horizontal document overflow.
No new console errors or animation-related warnings occur during five reload and navigation cycles.
expected_failure_modes: Below-fold content remains near-transparent when reduced motion is enabled.
Large groups reveal together and create a visible frame drop on mobile.
A fixed top bar overlaps an anchored heading at narrow widths.
notes: The user-required Framer layer is a documented exception to the lowest-engine preference. No smooth-scroll library is enabled.
